title: Personalized gene editing and rare diseases
text:
You want to read something inspiring, the best of humanity right here in Philadelphia?  A revolution is happening in genomics to cure rare diseases. The traditional model of pharma clinical trials and FDA approval is no longer relevant to these technologies, which need to be individualized to be patient-specific, much like what a surgeon does to fix a specific physical ailment. Our regulatory framework, and incentive structures, must adapt to be able to rapidly scale up these therapies. The idea is NOT to cut corners, but to be rigorous yet nimble.

As noted in this editorial, rare diseases are not rare at all in aggregate. I hope the flood gates for this will open wide!
